text: Shared page chrome rules (owner asked for consistency across the app, STA-660): (1) every page title (h1.pt) sits inside the .pagehead wrapper, which alone sets the 10px gap below the title; do not add per-page margins to fix title spacing. The design files show a bare h1 on notifications, new thread and comment form; the app wraps them on purpose. (2) Form errors use one style, the bordered .err box; the plain red-text .error class was removed. Considered and left alone by owner choice: the three empty-state text styles (normal text for 'No threads/notifications/results', grey for 'No comments yet', small mono hint for 'no invite links').
author: Stavros Korokithakis <hi@stavros.io>

text: Public mode scope (agreed with the owner, STA-644): visitors get read-only access to the thread list, threads and search only. Deliberately NOT public: the invite tree (/tree, /invites) because it exposes who invited whom; live SSE updates for visitors (avoid long-lived anonymous connections); per-thread visibility (rejected: turning public on retroactively exposes all old threads, accepted with a warning on the settings page instead); user profile pages (not built, would be a separate ticket). Settings live in the DB and are edited by admins rather than flags, because the owner wanted changes without a restart.
author: Stavros Korokithakis <hi@stavros.io>

text: The /account/api page (API documentation with the member's tokenized links) is not in misc/design/. It is a deliberate addition for STA-669, approved by the owner. It reuses the account page panel and kv styles. It is linked only from the feeds panel on the account page, not from the top navigation, on purpose: the navigation is part of the design and few members use the API.
author: Stavros Korokithakis <hi@stavros.io>

text: When @mention highlighting was added to the Markdown renderer (STA-640), stored body_html of old posts was NOT re-rendered, because the user confirmed no production server with real posts existed at the time. If highlights are missing on old posts in some database, that is why; a one-time re-render of threads.body_html and comments.body_html would fix it.
author: Stavros Korokithakis <hi@stavros.io>

text: The thread form (new and edit) deliberately puts the url field above the title, unlike misc/design/02-new-thread (owner request, STA-663): pasting a URL auto-fills an empty title from the page via POST /title. Do not restore title-first just because the design shows it. Scope agreed with the owner: og:title first, then <title>; the server refuses private/loopback/link-local addresses (owner wanted the guard even though members are invited). Observed Nov 2026: the production host is a data-centre IP, and YouTube serves it a bot-check page titled ' - YouTube' with no og:title, while YouTube's oEmbed API still works from there; home connections get the normal page, so this does not reproduce on a dev machine. Reddit serves a bot-check page titled 'Reddit'; nytimes.com returns 403. YouTube puts <title> about 840 KB into the page, which is why the read limit is 2 MB. The owner expects more site-specific exceptions soon, so they go in the per-site table in internal/linktitle/sites.go (custom title lookup such as oEmbed, plus junk titles that mean 'no title') rather than ad-hoc checks. The owner prefers a site's oEmbed API over page scraping wherever one exists (STA-663), so popular oEmbed sites are in the table; checked Nov 2026 and left out because their oEmbed has no title or needs auth: X/Twitter, Bluesky, Tumblr, Instagram, Facebook, CodePen, Kickstarter, Imgur, GitHub Gist, Twitch, Bandcamp; Mastodon has per-instance endpoints. Deliberately NOT built: generic oEmbed discovery, non-UTF-8 charset handling, caching, rate limiting, filling the body or images.
author: Stavros Korokithakis <hi@stavros.io>

text: The notifications panel (desktop alerts and ntfy) was added in STA-667 without a design. Since STA-671 it is part of the account design (misc/design/07-account). Deviations kept on purpose (owner, STA-671): the ntfy checkbox reads 'replies, comments and mentions' instead of the design's 'replies and mentions', because the setting covers all personal notifications; the desktop alerts pill also shows 'off', 'blocked by the browser' and 'not supported', which the design does not show.
author: Stavros Korokithakis <hi@stavros.io>

text: The design in misc/design shows the footer as 'soliloquy v1.0 · AGPL-3.0 · source · invite tree'. The app deliberately shows only 'powered by soliloquy', linked to the GitHub repo (owner decision, STA-656). Reasons: the version was hardcoded and always wrong, the invite tree link duplicates the main nav, and the GitHub link already covers source and license. Rejected: a real build version via -ldflags or debug.ReadBuildInfo (build plumbing for little value). The footer still shows only to logged-in users. Do not restore the old items just because the design shows them.
author: Stavros Korokithakis <hi@stavros.io>

text: The front page design (misc/design/00-front-page and the mobile screen) shows 'sorted by latest activity · page N' next to the ~/threads heading, and a mobile row 'latest activity / page N'. Both were deliberately removed (owner decision, STA-656): there is only one sort order, and the page number repeats the bottom bar. The bottom pagination bar ('page N of M · 30 per page' with newer/older buttons) is also hidden when there is no other page to go to, because it then has no buttons. Do not restore these labels just because the design shows them.
author: Stavros Korokithakis <hi@stavros.io>

text: The design in misc/design shows a 'mark all as read' button on the notifications page. It was deliberately left out (user decision, STA-640): opening the page keeps marking everything read, and the 'unread' section shows what was unread before the visit. Rejected alternative: mark one item read only on click, plus the button; it needs a GET link that changes data and adds a step for users. Do not add the button just because the design shows it.
author: Stavros Korokithakis <hi@stavros.io>

text: JSON API (STA-669, agreed with the owner): read-only /api/threads (front page order and paging) and /api/threads/{id} (thread with nested comment tree, Markdown and HTML bodies). Access reuses the RSS feed rule and the per-user feed token on purpose: same read-only grant, no new token, column or UI. Rejected: Reddit-style .json suffix on page URLs (router treats the suffix as part of the ID, front page cannot take one); separate API token or Bearer header. Out of scope: writes and votes, CORS, rate limiting, recent-comments list, newest-first sort, search/notification/user endpoints, versioning.
author: Stavros Korokithakis <hi@stavros.io>

text: Panels with class 'panel account-section' (admin settings, API docs) are app additions with no design file. Since STA-671 the account page no longer uses them; it has its own card layout from misc/design/07-account, and the owner chose to keep admin settings and API docs on the old panel style for now (they now look different from the account page on purpose). Owner approved one spacing rule for these panels (STA-670): 12px between blocks, 8px above a hint (the value misc/design uses for the hint on the invites page), 10px below the panel heading, 18px between panels. Rejected: one 12px gap for everything, because it moves hints away from the control they explain. Considered and left alone by owner choice: button heights differ on purpose (32px default, 36px thread form, 28px copy, full width on auth pages), they come from the design, do not unify them; dl.kv lists inside these panels render in the sans font while the same list in the 'whoami' box is mono.
author: Stavros Korokithakis <hi@stavros.io>

text: Static assets linked from layout.html get a content hash in the filename (/static/style.<hash>.css) and are served immutable for a year (owner decision, STA-660). Origin: after a deploy the owner still saw an old stylesheet; the app sent no cache headers and reused the same URL. Owner chose hashed filenames over the proposed ?v=<hash> query marker. Also rejected: Cache-Control: no-cache on static files (a request per page load, and some CDNs ignore it). Deliberately not hashed: static/fonts/* (style.css links them by absolute URL, so hashing needs CSS rewriting at startup, and they do not change) and /favicon.ico (fixed conventional path). Unhashed /static/ URLs still work on purpose, for the fonts and for /static/og.png links that other sites may hold. If a font file is ever replaced, give it a new file name.
author: Stavros Korokithakis <hi@stavros.io>

text: Notification channels model (STA-667, agreed with the owner): three kinds of notification, (1) new threads, (2) all new comments, (3) replies to me (the in-app notifications: reply, thread_comment, mention). Shared channels configured by the admin (Discord webhooks) carry only kinds 1-2, never kind 3. Personal channels: RSS (all three kinds; /feeds/notifications added for kind 3), browser desktop alerts (kind 3 only, while a tab is open, per-browser setting in localStorage, not in the DB), ntfy push (kind 3 on by default, kind 1 opt-in, never kind 2). Kind 2 stays RSS-only because pushing every comment is too noisy. Rejected: a full per-user kind x channel settings grid (YAGNI); Web Push/VAPID, Telegram and email (much more work, little gain; email is also a PRD non-goal). ntfy decisions from the owner: the user enters any https topic URL for any server, including self-hosted ones; the owner accepts that members can make the server POST to arbitrary https hosts. Pushes include the thread title and actor but not the comment body; the owner said users must pick hard-to-guess topic names. Like Discord, ntfy has no retries or queue.
author: Stavros Korokithakis <hi@stavros.io>

text: The feeds panel (tokenized RSS URLs and a reset button) was added in STA-666 without a design. Since STA-671 it is part of the account design ('feeds and API' card in misc/design/07-account).
author: Stavros Korokithakis <hi@stavros.io>

text: The account (misc/design/07-account), notifications (03, 820px), search (04, 780px, centred) and comment form (820px) pages had narrower columns in the design. The app deliberately uses the normal 960px page column on all of them, so their boxes are as wide as the admin pages and header (owner decision, STA-660). The narrower caps were mostly left-aligned, which left empty space on the right and looked broken. Rejected: centring the narrow columns to match the design (the owner wanted full width). Not changed: the 72ch reading width of thread bodies. Input widths on the account page (superseded STA-671): the new account design (misc/design/07-account, STA-671) makes the ntfy URL and feed URL inputs full width and caps the password inputs and the delete confirmation input at 340px; the app follows it (owner approved). The earlier STA-670 full-width password inputs and the 220px inline delete input are gone. Do not restore the narrow page caps just because the design shows them.
author: Stavros Korokithakis <hi@stavros.io>

text: Discord integration scope (agreed with the owner, STA-659): every new thread (not only link threads) posts one plain-text message to each admin-configured webhook URL; multiple webhooks were requested by the owner. Body is included but cut to 300 characters because the owner did not want Discord to be spammy. Plain text chosen over Discord embeds for simplicity. Link previews are also turned off (SUPPRESS_EMBEDS flag, STA-665): the owner found them useless. The flag was chosen over wrapping links in <> because it also covers URLs in the body excerpt. Deliberately NOT built: posting comments, edits or deletes; retries or a delivery queue (a lost message is acceptable); per-webhook options; Slack/generic webhooks; a host allowlist (only admins set URLs). Webhooks are configured in DB settings, not env vars, to match the no-restart rule in bedjup. The message does not include the external URL of link threads (STA-661): the owner wants Discord members to visit the forum to see the link and talk about it there.
author: Stavros Korokithakis <hi@stavros.io>

text: RSS feeds (STA-666, agreed with the owner): RSS 2.0 feeds for new threads and for all new comments (one forum-wide comment feed, no per-thread feeds), 50 newest items each, sorted by creation time not activity. Private forums authenticate feeds with a per-user secret token in the URL query, shown on the account page with a reset button. The token is stored in plain text on purpose: it only grants read access to content that is already in the database, and plain text lets the account page show the URL again. Rejected: HTTP Basic Auth with the real password (readers store it, poor reader support, login throttle interplay); hashed token (URL visible only once). Owner requirement: a tokenized feed URL must keep working when the forum is switched public and back to private, so the account page always shows the tokenized URLs, and a valid token is always accepted regardless of the public setting. Out of scope: Atom/JSON Feed, per-user feeds other than notifications, search feeds, token expiry. STA-667 superseded the earlier 'no notification feeds' rule: /feeds/notifications is a personal feed of the user's in-app notifications. It needs a valid token or session even on a public forum, and is not advertised with rel=alternate.
author: Stavros Korokithakis <hi@stavros.io>

text: Favicon and OG image (STA-647, user decision): one static text-free mark (amber chevron + cursor on #0f110e) for all forums. Rejected: baking 'soliloquy' into og.png (wrong after an admin renames the forum); rendering a per-forum OG image in Go (needs a TTF font, a font dependency and a handler, too much for a preview image); a favicon SVG that switches colours with the system theme (the ICO/PNG cannot switch, fixed dark tile reads fine on both). No og:description on purpose: the app has no description text and a fixed sentence would be wrong for most forums.
author: Stavros Korokithakis <hi@stavros.io>

text: STA-671 account redesign: misc/design/07-account.html and .png were replaced with the owner's new account design (from a new design export; the other screens in misc/design and misc/design_reference.html were not updated). Owner decisions: the theme applies at once and saves in the background (no-JS save button kept); the section menu highlight follows scrolling; account deletion now also clears the ntfy URL and feed token so the delete text is true. Kept although the design does not show them: the .err box under the page title and the ntfy test result notice. Footer stays 'powered by soliloquy' (see gxrrmu).
author: Stavros Korokithakis <hi@stavros.io>

text: The desktop design (misc/design/05-invites-and-invite-tree.png) shows the 'invite someone' and 'your links' panels both below the invite tree. The app deliberately puts 'invite someone' above the tree and keeps 'your links' below it (owner decision, STA-649): the tree grows with each member and would push the main action of the page down. Rejected: a sidebar next to the tree (too cramped in the 960px page, even after widening it from 280px to 320px); both panels above the tree (the link history grows and would push the tree down). The same order is used on mobile. The mobile design (13) has no 'your links' list and a different invite box style; matching that was left out of scope.
author: Stavros Korokithakis <hi@stavros.io>

text: Admins can edit any thread (title, URL, body) but NOT comments (owner decision, STA-654): the main need is fixing bad titles, and editing other people's comments has more room for abuse. Admin edits show only 'edited' with no editor name; an 'edited by admin' marker (needs a DB column) was deferred until it is a real problem. Thread edit/delete sit in the meta line ('2 comments · edited · edit · delete'); the design has no thread controls, and the owner finds 'edited' next to the controls a bit odd but accepted it for now.
author: Stavros Korokithakis <hi@stavros.io>
